subject: Don't set the mouse cursor for items that are disabled
description: Don't set the mouse cursor for items that are disabled  As with widgets, items that are disabled should not receive any input events.  Similar to QGraphicsScene, which ignores disabled items when handling mouse presses, the view should also ignore them when handling mouse moves to update the cursor.  Since QGraphicsView only adjusts the cursors on mouse moves, reenabling an item that is currently under the mouse will not change the cursor. This is consistent with other changes of item attributes that would position the item under the mouse (such as moving it). The overhead of hit-testing items for every such attribute change would be too large, and applications can generate a mouse move event if they really need to adjust the cursor in all situations.  [ChangeLog][QtWidgets][QGraphicsView] Ignore disabled items when setting the mouse cursor.  Change-Id: Ifcd31fc0581e8421e58eeb436a55b031909eed7e

subject: Add a tech preview eglfs device integration for VSP2 composition
description: WIP: Add an eglfs device integration for VSP2 composition  This creates a new device integration for eglfs, eglfs_kms_vsp2, that's very similar to eglfs_kms_gbm, but includes an extra step for doing VSP2 hardware compositing.  The main Qt content is drawn to double buffered off-screen GBM buffers which are converted using drmPrimeHandleToFD so we get DMA buffer file descriptors that can be used by the VSP2 blending hardware. The blending hardware writes to double buffered DRM dumb buffers, which are flipped with drmModePageFlip.  Communicating with the VSP2 is done using the Video4Linux2 (V4L2) streaming API. There are two steps in creating abstractions for this. First, there is the QLinuxMedia class that consists of a Qt style wrapper for V4L2 without anything VSP2 specific. Second, there is QVsp2BlendingDevice which hides some of the streaming details of the VSP2 and has some level of error recovery. Both classes include a fair bit of logging and error reporting.  The patch is written with Wayland compositors in mind, but should work for other use cases as well.  TODO:  - Clients are not flushed to the screen unless the compositor updates. Clients   should also be able to cause the blending unit to blend and the display to   flip. - Support the client setting the alpha value of a layer. - There's a bug when reconnecting after a client leaves (size is not set   properly...) - Reduce duplications (many files are just simple copies from eglfskmsgbm). - I've totally ignored cursors and just copied what was in eglfskmsgbm. It   probably doesn't work. - Support foreign layers below the main Qt layer. - Rename QLinuxMedia and/or QVsp2BlendingDevice? - Move VSP2 functions from eglfsfunctions.h to somewhere else? - Log to new logging category(ies)? - Remove dead code that was only needed by eglfskmsgbm. - VSP2 and V4L2 feature detection is untested on non-VSP2 devices and not used   everywhere. - Go through latest patches for eglfskms and see if something applies to this   patch as well (i.e. drmModeAddFB2 and similar)  Missing nice-to-haves:  - Support clipping layers. - Support for scaling layers. - Support for other output formats than RGBA32. - Support for memory mapped and user pointer buffer types (currently only DMA   buffers are supported). - Support for multi-planar buffers? (currently we use multi-planar buffers with   just one plane)  Change-Id: I1917d2dbdbaeded0d9c021baaa799d56afe1a9bd

subject: qdoc: A different way to fix the "signed" problem
description: qdoc: A different way to fix the "signed" problem  The old qdoc parser is still used for parsing \fn commands because clang can't be used to parse code fragments. This causes a problem when the "signed" reserved word is used because clang doesn't keep it if it doesn't add anything to the type, while the old qdoc parser always appends it to the type under construction.  The fix here is to let the old qdoc parser hold the "signed" reserved word aside until it knows what the next lexeme is. Then it either appends the held "signed" or discards it, depending on what the next lexeme is. e.g., if the next word is "int" discard "signed" but if the next word is "char" append the held "signed" before appending "char".  Change-Id: I67953d964cd09410126d64fa3305c669111e74ce

subject: Add a macro to disable only some 8 bit/16 bit string conversions
description: Add a macro to disable only some 8 bit/16 bit string conversions  This is an opt-in trade-off between type safety and user code convenience.  QT_NO_CAST_FROM_ASCII is highly beneficial to avoid unintended conversions from 8 bit data with potentially "unsuitable" encodings to QString. However, it has the undesirable side-effect to require user code to wrap character and string literals in QLatin1Char(...) and QLatin1String(...) or use similar construction, cluttering the code significantly.  This patch introduces a QT_ALMOST_NO_CAST_FROM_ASCII macro that works almost as QT_NO_CAST_FROM_ASCII, except that it enables the QChar(char) constructors and adds an additional QString(const char (&ch)[N]) constructor that matches C++ string literals, but no arbitrary character pointers. This avoids a significant share of the need to clutter the user code by only a slight relaxation of the type-safety.  [ChangeLog][QtNetwork][QString] Added QT_ALMOST_NO_CAST_FROM_ASCII macro as less intrusive alternative to QT_NO_CAST_FROM_ASCII.  Change-Id: Iac72f1f90f81fbcae9bfb1fe68b0fec6ffb36c50

subject: Provide calendar backends with a unique ID
description: Provide calendar backends with a unique ID  A backend whose name was already in use would previously not have been registred at all, meaning that the code that created it would need to be responsible for deleting it, and nothing would be able to use it.  The code that created it would, furthermore, have no way to know this (other than by detecting differences in behaviour between the backend it thought it had registered and a QCalendar instantiated using its name). This meant that the creator of a backend that fell foul of this would most likely leak the backend.  Registration by ID also allows for detection of duplicate instantiation of built-in back-ends, which can be detected and flagged by setting the ID to ~size_t(0) instead of the enum value for which it sought to be registered. A new method, calendarId(), is provided to access this; while the old calendarSystem() becomes non-virtual, as it can be inferred (when registration was successful) from the ID.  [ChangeLog][QtCore][QCalendar] QCalendarBackend::calendarSystem() is no longer virtual; instead, each backend is assigned an ID when registred as part of its creation, from which calendarSystem() can be inferred. The ID is unique except in the case of duplicate registration of backends for which a built-in implementation exists, when ~size_t(0) is used as ID, to let client code know the backend it has just created has not been registred properly.  Change-Id: Ib22925a8ac3ef9439a09ec3855f6231cf9b91c21

subject: Add Singleton support for QML
description: WIP: Add initial Singleton support for QML  This is the initial stab at introducing Singleton support for QML. You define a type as a Singleton by adding the following to your types QML file:  pragma Singleton  Currently the pragma needs to be before any import statement. The goal is to be able to have them mixed. Singleton is the only supported pragma for now. Others will generate errors.  The problem with the current implementation is that the QML files using a Singleton type need to resolve the type and have it in their typecache. As the Singleton is used as a value to properties, or as part of a javascript block, it is very difficult to detect if a type needs to be resolved. Up to now we have not validated the contents of property values and javascript blocks at the parser level.  In this change I've only hooked up the bool ProcessAST::visit(AST::UiPublicMember *node) to look for something that looks like a Singleton type (with an uppercase first letter). However, this is not scalable as we do not want to do string pattern matching to find a candidate. There needs to be a better way to handle this.  I used "qlalr --no-debug --no-lines --qt qqmljs.g" to generate the qqmljsparser and qqmljsgrammar files from qqmljs.g.  There are no unit tests attached yet to this WIP patch.  Change-Id: I91b303612c5e132143b325b9a8f982e9355bc90e

subject: qdoc: Reorganize Qdoc's Node class hierarchy
description: qdoc: Find the c and c++ include dirs for macOS  This update is required because the libclang release packages listed on the Qt Downloads page don't include the c and c++ header files that are provided by the LLVM builder.  When I buildt my own LLVM for version 3.9, it installed the clang libraries and include files and the c and c++ headers in /usr/local. All I had to do was set LLVM_INSTALL_DIR to /usr/local, and qdoc would build and run as expected. The clang parser used in qdoc would find the c and c++ include files in /usr/local/include.  When it came time to upgrade my clang to version 6.0, I installed the libclang release package for macOS, which creates a libclang directory with the clang libraries and clang headers, but not the c and c++ headers. So when I set LLVM_INSTALL_DIR to that libclang dir, it built qdoc ok, but when I ran qdoc, it printed thousands of errors for missing c++ and c types, because the include directories passed to qdoc on the command line don't include anything for finding the c and c++ headers.  qdoc detects now -clang-path parameters on the command line. It uses these two paths into the macOS SDK to construct these two include paths, which lead to the c++ and c include directories respectively:  -I/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/include/c++/v1 -I/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX10.14.sdk/usr/include  This works on my mac, except for the "variant" template used in one place in qvariant.h, where clang says there is no template named variant in namespace std. However, there is a template named variant in the <variant> header, but clang in qdoc is not seeing it, which might be revealing a problem with this update. Namely, the clang version in my libclang directory is different from the clang version in my macOS SDK, so maybe the c and c++ headers in the SDK are not compatible with the clang in my libclang. If that is the problem, then maybe our libclang-release packages on the Qt Downloads page should go the extra step of including the c and c++ headers that are made available when each LLVM is built.  Change-Id: I918f83030c48d96db4a5588ab53458f221a5374e

description: WIP: Add qgltf tool  This tool, integrated with qmake, converts anything assimp imports into a subset of glTF. Techniques, render passes, shaders, and such are excluded - these are better specified in QML (as that's why we have Qt 3D in the first place). subject: Build examples in isolated sub-builds using ExternalProject
description: Build examples as tests rather than as part of the main build  Examples are intended to show how to build against an installed Qt. Building them as part of the main build means the way the Qt targets are defined and created are not representative of an end user's build. By building them as tests instead, we more closely replicate the intended audience's environment. This should allow us to catch more problems earlier.  Having examples built as part of the main build also creates problems with some static builds where a tool built by the main build is needed during configure time. This happens with other repos like qtdeclarative but not (currently) with qtbase. Converting the examples in qtbase to be built as tests is intended as a demonstrator for how other repos can do similar. Until other repos are converted, they will continue to call qt_examples_build_begin() and therefore continue to not build examples for static builds. Once they have been converted, they should remove their calls to qt_examples_build_begin() and qt_examples_build_end(), which will then allow their example tests to be built in static builds as well.  For efficiency reasons, the examples are grouped by default instead of making each one its own separate test case. The cost of generating a new CMake build directory is non-trivial with some CMake generator types (notably Xcode and Visual Studio). The groupings in this commit are intended as a balanced tradeoff between test granularity and build efficiency, but an option is provided to allow developers to disable grouping.  Task-number: QTBUG-90820 Fixes: QTBUG-91068 Pick-to: 6.1 Change-Id: I2304329940568dbdb7da18d54d5595ea7d8668bc

subject: qmldom: Add Path and ErrorMessage to Dom
description: Adding Path and ErrorMessage to Dom  Adds more groundwork for the Dom library.  QQml::Dom::Path represents a path in the Dom model. It goes from an element of the Dom model (DomItem) to another.  It can be created either from a string, with the path static functions or by modifying an existing path  Path qmlFilePath =     Path::fromString(u"$env.qmlFilesByPath[\"/path/to/file\"]"); Path imports = qmlFilePath.subField(u"imports") Path currentComponentImports = Path::current(u"component")         .subField(u"imports");  This is a way to refer to elements in the Dom models that is not dependent from the source location, and thus can be used also be used in visual tools. A Path is quite stable toward reallocations or changes in the Dom model, and accessing it is safe even when "dangling", thus it is a good long term reference to an element in the Dom model.  In this commit the element of the Dom Model (DomItem) is represented just by a stub object, it will be added in a subsequent commit.  This commit also introduces the ErrorMessage object. ErrorMessage is an object used to represent error, warning and other messages in the Dom model. Errors are grouped by tags (ErrorGroups). ErrorMessages might have a unique identifying string (using a number in a base library that cannot have a list of all possible errors does not work well. ErrorMessages should be localized and *can* be pre-registred, but do not have to be. ErrorMessages can be associated with a QQml::Dom::Path, a file and a Sourcelocation. The path (if present) might allows one to show errors also in more visual tools.  Task-number: QTBUG-74840 Change-Id: I77fb4b78e15ba3674d74937106d40dba4076cedc

The output of this pass is an MIFunction (MI = Machine Interface), which uses a representation suitable for feeding to an assembler. subject: Transient QWindows centered; default-constructed geometry
description: Transient QWindows centered; default-constructed geometry  Default-constructed geometry does not mean put the window at 0,0, and it does not mean center the window on the screen: it means let the window manager position the window.  If the window is explicitly positioned at 0,0 though, that is a higher priority than the transient hint; without this change, the transientFor property had no effect.  On X11, transient means use center "gravity" to make the transient window exactly centered.  But the user can still override the geometry of a transient window, as with any window. On OSX and Windows, neither transient window functionality nor smart initial positioning are provided, so a window with no position set will be centered on the screen, and a transient window will be put at the center of its transientParent.  Change-Id: I4f5e37480eef5d105e45ffd60362a57f13ec55f5 Task-number: QTBUG-26903

subject: Track grab state in QPointingDevicePrivate::activePoints
description: WIP Track grab state by keeping active point instances in QPointingDevice  QQuickEventPoint instances were very long-lived and got reused from one event to the next.  That was initially done because they were "heavy" QObjects; but it also became useful to store state in them between events.  So to continue using the same principle for the benefit of delivery code in QQuickWindow, it's useful for QEventPoint instances to live at least as long as the gesture from press to release. For example, setExclusiveGrabber() has been there since 4e400369c08db251cd489fec1229398c224d02b4, but the grabber would need to be "remembered" elsewhere between events if we did not keep the QEventPoint instance itself.  QGuiApplication now uses the instances stored in QPointingDevice, and we ensure that they are always passed by reference, never copied, so that when the eventual event handler changes grabbers, that will be remembered between events.  The grabChanged() signal is useful to keep QQuickWindow informed when items or handlers change exclusive or passive grabbers.  Change-Id: I2733d847139a1b1bea33c00275459dcd2a145ffc

subject: Implement command prefix
description: WIP: Implement command prefix  The current CI magically add prefix to every executed command if target compiler is MSVC. The prefix just calls vcvarsall.bat. The script has to be called for every command, because of the CI agent runs every command as a subprocess. It means that script sourced environment is not passed to subsequent commands, therefore all changes are lost.  The prefix, as a concept, has known performance issues (COIN-253), so in long term it would be nice to move to another solution.  CustomModule doesn't support prefix. Therefore the proposed approach moves the ugliness from CI code to the yaml configuration file. It has two advantages; nothing needs to be implemented on the CI level and hopefully someone in future will clean it up as the problem is more visible and publicly fixable. description: WIP: Support Pointer Primitive Types by Result Tuples  Most primitive types are handled in XML, but this is not reflected by the signatures, error messages, doc strings and hinting stubs.  In order to enhance the information shown to be more correct, the C++ parser was completely rewritten for Python. It is closely written to Python syntax, but keeps the existing information about primitive types intact.  In the C implementation, pointer variables are turned into result tuples that can hold multiple values. To create a correct Python display of those variables, the signatures must be re-written, accordingly. We apply the transformations automatically:  A constant expression like      const thing*  is clearly not a variable and is handled as bytes or List[thing] .  In case of      thing*  it is not always clear if a variable or an array is meant. We resolve that by a table which uses the variable name as an indicator. A small number (5) of variables are still unnamed, and they are explicitly resolved. description: WIP: Long live std::pair!  Make QPair an alias for std::pair, and qMakePair just a forwarder towards std::make_pair.  Why? Fundamentally to ditch a bunch of NIH code; gain for free structured bindings, std::tuple and std::reference_wrapper compatibility, and so on. There are a handful of these in qtbase, but only one was actually broken.  * std::pair is NOT (and will never likely be) trivially copiable. This is agreed to be a mistake done by practically all implementations in C++11, can can't be fixed without breaking ABI. subject: WebGradients: redo implementation
description: WebGradients: redo implementation  The previous implementation was *extremely* expensive. It relied on loading a binary JSON file from resources, then extracting information out of it to build a gradient. Already-loaded gradients were kept in a local cache, which had to be mutex protected.  Instead, this patch extends the gradient generator to build an array of QGradients with the web gradient data. This array is used when building QGradient objects with a web gradient. No explicit mutex protection is necessary, since accesses will just read from the array; Q_GLOBAL_STATIC gives us what we need (lazy loading of it, in a thread safe way).  As benefits, this patch removes:  * a *WHOPPING* 50KB from QtGui's .rodata (the binary json is dropped) * the overhead of parsing the JSON for each used web gradient; * the startup costs of registering the webgradients in the resources; * all the overhead of mutex locking when building such gradients; * all the runtime memory allocations to load, parse and cache the web gradients.  The cost of keeping the entire array allocated is completely negligible since we were keeping the entire binary JSON in memory anyhow (11K of statically allocated data vs 50K of heap allocated data), plus the cache that we don't need anymore.  Change-Id: If5c3d704430df76ce8faf55ee75ebd4639ba09c4

subject: Expose video surfaces in rendering components
description: Introduce QVideoWidget::surface()  Currently QVideoWidget is supposed to be used strongly with QMediaPlayer via QMediaPlayer::setVideoOutput(QVideoWidget *), but both QMediaPlayer and QVideoWidget are based on QMediaService and QMediaControl.  E.g. QVideoWidget::setMediaObject() is called to provide the media service of QMediaPlayer and its controls, such as QVideoRendererControl, which provides a possibility to get video frames from a backend.  Introducing QVideoWidget::surface() that creates if necessary and returns underlaying video surface which provides a possibility to render video frames without knowledge of any services and controls.  Could be tried like:   QMediaPlayer->setVideoOutput(QVideoWidget->surface());  which allows QMediaPlayer to get video frames from a backend, without using QVideoWidget, and presents these frames to widget's surface.  More over, now it is possible to render video frames to QVideoWidget without QMediaPlayer:   QVideoSurfaceFormat format(img.size(), QVideoFrame::Format_ARGB32);   videoWidget->surface()->start(format);   videoWidget->surface()->present(img);  This removes dependency to QMediaService and QMediaControl.  [ChangeLog] Introduced QVideoWidget::surface()  Task-number: QTBUG-74422 Change-Id: I49641750537160832e29c297279e72b8288e974c

subject: qWaitFor: Prevent being stuck in QCoreApplication::processEvents
description: qWaitFor: Prevent being stuck in QCoreApplication::processEvents  When using the overload of QCoreApplication::processEvents that takes a maxtime argument, the function will keep processing events until there are no more events, or until it times out.  The problem is that the function doesn't distinguish between events that were on the event queue when the function was called, and events generated by processing events as part of its own execution. If for example a widget calls update() in its paintEvent, the function will spin for the entire duration of maxtime.  That doesn't work for qWaitFor, where we need to check the predicate between each pass, so we use the overload of processEvents that doesn't take a maxtime. That's fine, as we have our own timeout logic.  Change-Id: I9738d7d0187c36d4a5ddfcd3fd075b0bd84583c4

subject: Use sysfs on Linux when available
description: WIP: Linux: Refuse the filter of names of serial ports at enumeration  For listing of devices (if OS has no libudev) the search on a mask in directory "/dev" was used. For this purpose we had some database - the filters list of masks of names of devices that guaranteed the matchings.  But this decision had shortcomings:  For different Linux versions of kernels (for example for embedded customizations of different ARM, MIPS and so forth MCU's) the devices have different names, therefore we were stimulated to add names of these devices into the list.  The solution of this problem is remove the list of filters, and for listing of devices to use directory "/sys/class/tty". To take of appropriate devices are used the predetermined names of subsystems (pnp, usb, etc.), as before.  I.e. this method works by the principle similar in libudev and doesn't require the rights of the superuser.  This patch - extension of ideas based on previous patch:  sha1: 4bdbbe4c87676ca94daae947ac5908d77966319b  Note:  Are possible some regressions relating to determination of rfcomm, ircomm devices. It needs to be checked and submitted the set of next patches to fix it.  Checked on Fedora 19 x64, Ubuntu 12 x32 with on-board (PnP) and pluggable (USB) devices.  Change-Id: Ia242bb2ed81d17b6f826a187454bb9d2a12d40a9

subject: Replace Qt's hashing function with SipHash
description: Replace Qt's hashing function with SipHash  This commit replaces both the standard DJB33XA (DJB's 33 Times Add) and the faster CRC32 hashing with SipHash. The most important difference between those algorithms is that both DJB33XA and CRC32 have this unwelcome property: for two byte sequences x and y, if you know that x and y have the same hashing for a given seed, then they have the same hashing for all seeds.  SipHash has no such issue. If the seed changes, the strings that used to compute to the same hash are no longer likely to do so.  We've chosen to implement a SipHash-1-2 algorithm instead of the regular 2-4 as that has roughly the same performance as the old DJB33XA algorithm. It's roughly 6x slower than the CRC32 algorithm, which will need a separate solution.  Change-Id: I09100678ff4443e6be06fffd14819c8878d223e2

subject: Improve support for applications that rely on fork for parallelism
description: Improve support for applications that rely on fork for parallelism  A forked process inherits the elfmap of the parent, thus we need to copy that data when we encounter a fork event. To do so reliably, we need to flush the event buffer, as otherwise the mmmap state may not be accurate.  Furthermore, pass the ppid through the ThreadStart event, to allow client applications to inherit the comm for the newly created process.  Fixes: https://github.com/KDAB/hotspot/issues/241 Change-Id: I5de13644e12def6704c5f622428a815fd87d2af4

subject: Support for LTTNG and ETW tracing
description: WIP: Support for LTTNG and ETW tracing.  This commit introduces minimal support for instrumentation within Qt. Currently, only LTTNG/Linux and ETW/Windows are supported.  The API consists of only three macros:      - Q_TRACE(tracepoint, args...)     - Q_DO_TRACE(tracepoint, args...)     - Q_TRACE_ENABLED(tracepoint)  When using LTTNG, Q_TRACE, Q_DO_TRACE and Q_TRACE_ENABLED map ultimately to tracepoint(), do_tracepoint() and tracepoint_enabled(), respectively. On ETW, Q_TRACE() and Q_DO_TRACE() are equivalent, ultimately amounting to a call to TraceLoggingWrite(), whereas Q_TRACE_ENABLED() wraps around TraceLoggingProviderEnabled().  A tracepoint provider is defined in a separate file, that follows the following format:      [provider_name]     tracepoint_name(arg_type, arg_name, ...)  For instance:      [qtcore]      qcoreapplication_ctor(int, argc, const char * const, argv)     qcoreapplication_foo(int, argc, const char[10], argv)     qcoreapplication_baz(const char[len], some_string, unsigned int, len)     qcoreapplication_qstring(const QString &, foo)     qcoreapplication_qrect(const QRect &, rect)  The provider file is then parsed by utils/tracegen/tracegen, which can be switched to output either ETW or LTTNG tracepoint definitions.  To use the above (inside qtcore), you need to include <private/qtraceevent_p.h>. After that, the following call becomes possible:      Q_TRACE(qcoreapplication_qrect, myRect);  Currently, all C++ primitive non-pointer types are supported for arguments. Additionaly, char * is supported, and is assumed to be a NULL-terminated string. Finally, a small subset of select Qt types (such as QString and QByteArray) are also supported. Dynamic arrays are supported using the syntax illustrated by qcoreapplication_baz above.  Change-Id: I59b48cf83acf5532a998bb493e6379e9177e14c8

subject: Long live QCborStreamWriter!
description: QJsonDocument: add support for encoding to CBOR  CBOR is the Concise Binary Object Representation, a very compact form of binary data encoding that is compatible with JSON. It's as concise as MessagePack (http://msgpack.org) but it is more regular and also has room for expansion. It's also more concise than BJSON and UBJSON, allowing for shorter message payloads.  See RFC 7049: http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7049.  Change-Id: Ia0aac2f09e9245339951ffff13c651cfeab77d3b

subject: Propagate synthesized mouse events in parallel with touch.
description: Propagate synthesized mouse events in parallel with touch.  The event propagation inside QQuickCanvas was to send the touch event through all elements and if it was accepted along the way stop. Afterwards generate a mouse event and propagate it through the items in the same way.  With this patch the behavior is changed instead to do the propagation in parallel. That means in paint order the items get sent a touch event and directly after the mouse event. Propagation stops if either is accepted.  A new unit test showing this behavior was added.  Change-Id: If19ef687d7602e83cc11b18d2fecfbbdb4e44f5c

subject: New qfloat16 class
description: initial submission of qfloat16 as a global class.  This constitutes a fairly complete submission of an entirely new floating point type which conforms to IEEE 754 as a 16-bit storage class.  Conversion between qfloat16 and float is fast, performed through a sequence of lookup tables.  Global-level functions qRound(), qRound64(), qFuzzyCompare(), qFuzzyIsNull(), qIsNull(), and qIntCast() each with a qfloat16 parameter have been included for completeness. subject: Implement distance field text rendering
description: WIP: Start of new text rendering  Mostly analysis and some work on separating out the font loading so far.  Thoughts: 1. Better isolation of loaded fonts while keeping compatibility. The current approach pollutes the main font database with fonts from specific presentations, which can cause a presentation to look different depending on what presentations were shown before it. We need to use QRawFont for loading the specific fonts of the project and let Qt do the normal font selection based on this preference.  2. Distance field rendering. Use the distance field cache and shaders from Qt Quick.  3. Keep the old text renderer behind some option, to avoid having to duplicate some of the logic, such as built-in drop shadows, which are probably better handled in a more generic way.  4. Lookups currently done on the font file name, which is probably inherited from Qt 3D Studio 1 and required for compatibility. It is also useful to provide a way to directly use a specific font file, something which is currently missing from Qt Quick.  5. The current update logic will always redo the text. This is of course inefficient, but it means we don't have to worry too much about optimizing this path.  6. Selections or styled text do not seem to be supported in the current approach which limits the scope, thankfully.  7. Should be flexible enough that we can add stuff like elide and formatting later on, since users are bound to request this as soon as they realize it isn't supported.  8. The font selection seems to be exclusively based on loading a specific font file currently. In a cross-platform environment you will probably want more indirect ways of querying fonts, like QFont, but that is also not required in the first version it seems.  Change-Id: I6df62a85ca0ec61609504c929b9c3d126719ba48

subject: Implement theming for QtCreator
description: Implement a dark theme for QtCreator  Adds a '-dark' command line option, which switches QtCreator to a dark theme (for everything around the editor).  This does not use a stylesheet (too limited), but rather sets the palette via C++ and modifies drawing behaviour. Overall, the look is more flat (removed some gradients and bevels).  Tested on Ubuntu 14.04 using Qt 5.4 and running on a KDE Desktop (Oxygen base style).  For a screenshot, see https://gist.github.com/thorbenk/5ab06bea726de0aa7473  Currently, this is a proof of concept. See below for TODOs.  Changes: - Introduce Utils::StyleHelper::theme() to ask for the them   (currently: CreatorTheme_Original and CreatorTheme_Dark) - Add lots of if (dark) { } else { } to set certain colors,   tweak the drawing code etc - Create some custom icons which look better on dark background   (wip, currently folder/file icons) - Let ManhattanStyle draw some elements for non-panelwidgets, too   (open/close arrows in QTreeView, custom folder/file icons) - For QML's welcomescreen, pass a theme parameter  TODO: - Fix some more colors. Red (debugger), and Red/Blue (Compile Output)   are not too readable. - Fix some more icons - Test with different base styles other than Oxygen.  Change-Id: I92c2050ab0fb327649ea1eff4adec973d2073944

subject: feature-select: allow snake_case instead of camelCase for methods
description: WIP: pythonic: allow lower_case instead of camelCase for functions  This is an experimental feature: We want to study how lower_case functions would feel in PySide2. It may be that people are fine with the new names. But it is also possible that we need a more sophisticated algorithm than to just replace an upper case name by _lower case.  The interesting challenge is that the decision of a functions visibility needs to be computed from which module is currently active.  The decision depends of the following setting at the beginning of a module:      from PySide2.__future__ import lower_case  Task-number: PYSIDE-1019 Change-Id: I5f103190be2c884b0b4ad806187f3fef8e6598c9

subject: Implement introspection with __signature__ package
description: WIP: Implement introspection  This is the first _working_ version of some PySide introspection. We are using an enhanced version of PyCFunction_Type, modelled after the Cython implementation.  The current version uses only single signatures and adds the new properties to the PySide builtin function type. This is for a first, easy introspection and to put the final touch on the new feature.  We will then build two separate function types for single and multiple signatures that live in an own module and only exist for the signature info. An extra python module is then needed to show the signatures.  ToDo: - finish the type initialization - remove the modified type and create two shadow-types, instead.  Remark: I am not so sure if I want to change the principle, again: It seems to be sufficient to have the signatures as they are. For multiple signatures, I thing we can do with a simple iterator. This is a bit in flux, right now.  Example usage:  >>> import PySide2.QtWidgets >>> import inspect >>> inspect.signature(PySide2.QtWidgets.QGraphicsAnchorLayout().addAnchors)  Task-number: PYSIDE-510 Change-Id: Ibb231a7fbb4ccc1a7249df55e3881a4e21a19c0d

subject: QWindow::destroy(): only reset QGuiApp::focus_window and friends as a last resort
description: QWindow::destroy(): only reset QGuiApp::focus_window and friends as a last resort  Resetting focus_window and other internal QGuiApplication variables before calling setVisible(false) and destroying the platform window means that the platform window can't reason about whether or not it was the focus window unless it can resolve that using native APIs. We should let the platform window take care of resetting the focus window and related states, and only execute our fallback logic if the plugin doesn't do the right thing.  We also use QPA to update the state instead of modifying the internal QGuiApplication variables directly, so that events and signals are emitted as a result of the reset.  The flush in the QPlatformWindow destructor is needed so that we can reason about focus_window after destroying the platform window, but also makes sense in general.  Change-Id: I562788393ed0ffd77d7a4be2279862322f721c1a

subject: Linux: Add abstract address support for QLocal{Socket,Server}
description: Linux: QLocalSocket & Server support abstract socket  This patch is also valid for Android. When QLocalServer is started with WorldAccessOption set the socket created will be an abstract one. Any other option of the server implies creating a regular socket. QLocalSocket, on the other hand, attempts to connect to an abstract socket, and if it fails, starts connecting to a non-abstract one. subject: Long live QStringView!
description: WIP: Long live QStringView!  QStringView is a simple container for (const QChar*, int) and (const char16_t*, size_t), respectively. It acts as a replacement interface type for const QString, const QStringRef, and QChar, and enables passing all kinds of string-like types to functions otherwise expecting const QString& - without the need to convert to QString first.  The use of this new class is guarded by a macro that enables four levels of QStringView support:   0. offer no QStringView  1. offer QStringView, overload some functions taking     QString with QStringView  2. like 0, but remove all overloads of functions taking     QString, QStringRef, QChar, leaving only the function     taking QStringView. Do this only where QStringRef/QChar     overloads tradionally existed.  3. like 1, but replace functions that traditionally didn't     overload on QStringRef, too.  This is done in order to measure the impact of QStringView on code size and execution speed, and to help guide the decision of which level to choose for Qt 6.  This first patch adds QStringView with all its constructors, but nothing more than relational operations, iterators and isNull()/isEmpty().  Further patches will add support for QStringView to QStringBuilder, add QStringView overloads of functions taking QString, and add the complete API of const QString to QStringView.  Change-Id: Iac273e46b2c61ec2c31b3dacebb29500599d6898

subject: Add support for calendars beside Gregorian
description: WIP: Adding Calendar System classes and Jalali Calendar  QAbstractCalendar class has been added as a base class for calendar implementations. This class contains several information on the underlying calendar.  QDate member functions modified to take a reference to calendar object. Original implementations still exist in code.  QLocale integration with QAbstractCalendar is completed by adding several functions. As for QDate, original functions are there. subject: Simplify fileTimeToQDateTime() by having it return a UTC time

The prior code, using SystemTimeToTzSpecificLocalTime(), lead to unhelpful results when the QDateTime() implementation used MS-POSIX's defective mktime(). Although SystemTimeToTzSpecificLocalTime() is actually more correct, we were getting inconsistent results by mixing the two: and eliminating the use of mktime() turns out to be decidedly tricky.  So, to avoid inconsistency, stick with a UTC time (which is what FILETIME is defined as).  Change-Id: Ic0b99d25c4168f623d31967bc60665c0c4f38a14
